Arvanites Follow-Up

By: Kate Barry | Paid

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We go back to see why the Arvanites College of Education is still open.

Summary:
Despite a 12.5% matric pass rate in 2015, and the GDE notifying them in April 2016 of their intention to de-register the school, it's still business as usual at Arvanites. We hear more complaints from current parents, and ask the GDE why it's taking so long to implement their decision?

Further information:
We also hear more about Tony Arvanites, and why the school operates with a Savings Account in the name of his son Anthony?

Press Release:


Social Media Busting Crime
Could social media platforms be an ideal tool to track down and arrest criminals? Carte Blanche meets investigators using online platforms to connect communities and make it impossible for even the most cunning criminals to hide.


Script:


ARVANITES 2

V/O: Earlier this year we investigated the many complaints against Arvanites College of Education, - like last year’s dismal matric pass rate, when 14 out of 16 pupils failed.

Sheryl: I cannot be responsible for those kind of results.

Bongani: Who is responsible?

Sheryl: The learners and their parents.

Bongani: There was also the issue of the fake matric certificate issued to Benjamin Suttie.

Bongani: This is the real document. Some of these results do not match?

Bongani: I understand that some of these results do not match, but I don't know where they came from, who did what with them, I have no idea.

Cameron: When I first got there in Grade 8 and 9, if we were struggling in a test they literally would just give us the answers.

Bongani: The allegation is they are given the answers as they are writing the tests.

Sheryl: As they are writing the tests?

Bongani: Yes.

Sheryl: I don’t believe that is true for one minute.

V/O: They were also being taught by unqualified teachers, like Brenda Pieters and her twin daughters Kayla and Jeanine.

Cameron: They taught me Biology, they taught me Geography, taught me English.

V/O: The broadcast took many of the parents by surprise.

Farrah: I was shocked.

V/O: Farrah Menego has two children at the school, Chante and Austin

Farrah: I called my kids in and asked have you seen this? They said oh mom, that is like so the school.

Austin: Like with the exams that they were saying ja no that they gave answers, yes they would.

Chante: This term I was given answers in my Afrikaans and English tests when I was struggling and I asked Brenda for help.

Bongani: So what’s the school been like since the Carte Blanche story went out?

Chante: We would talk about Carte Blanche, Brenda would come in and say oh no they lied, they’re going to put an apology up next weekend maybe like a few seconds. And we would all watch CB and no one says an apology.

Farrah: Within that week after the airing my son was advised that his EGD drawings were 66 drawings behind. I mean hello, they are going to write Prelims in August, how can they be 66 drawings behind?

V/O: But after hearing the school’s teaching philosophy from Brenda Pieters, who has no teaching qualifications, it’s understandable.

Brenda: When a child comes home and says mom we did nothing today, trust me they did nothing, because we have those days. We are not super humans, I have bad hair days ok?

Jess: We don’t do anything in class. We sit there and if the Department comes in for example, Brenda will come in and just say act like you’re doing something.

V/O: Jess Higginson was in Grade 12 at Arvanites, but after watching the broadcast her parents did their homework.

Garry: My wife took Jess to a couple of colleges just to see as an alternative, and we were actually quite shocked to see how far she was behind in the curriculum. Jess has lost a year of her education. One principal even suggested she even go back to Grade 10 for the rest of this year, so it would set her back 2 years.

V/O: They took Jess out of Arvanites immediately without giving notice.

Jess: I don’t think that they deserve a proper reason for why I left. They don’t deserve it because they ruined my future basically. They’ve told me that I’m doing so well, they do all this stuff, and they make it seem as though like you’re clever. But then you have that self-conscious thing of what if I’m not actually clever enough? What if I can’t do the things that I thought I could do because they made it seem like that, but it’s not actually perceived as that? Because I’m actually below where I should be.

V/O: Jess is now waitressing and repeating Grade 11 with a private tutor. Chante and Austin are still at Arvanites because an alternative hasn’t been found.

On the 25th of April the Gauteng Department of Education issued a letter of intention to withdraw the school’s registration. But 2 months later when Carte Blanche visited Arvanites we found it was business as usual and the Grade 12s were writing matric exams.

Bongani link: We asked Arvanites College for an interview and were told they’re not available for the next 3 weeks because they’re busy marking exam papers. They did confirm they sent a response to the Department on the 23rd of May, and they say they haven’t heard anything since.

V/O: And when we approached the Department for a status update, they weren’t very forthcoming either.

Bongani link: The GDE didn’t have much to say except that they have received a written response from Arvanites College and that the matter remains with their legal team. But they were unwilling to go on the record for an on camera interview.

Bongani: If you could speak to Sheryl what would you say?

Jess: I would tell her that she’s selfish and money hungry for taking all these kids school fees and not giving them what they deserve. Because that is the one thing that you are entitled to, is an education, and they just took that from your hands.
